questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Zimbabwe about 390,757 square kilometres; Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres; Comoros about 2,034 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Zimbabwe?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zimbabwe article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Zimbabwe?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the Zimbabwe article.

questions.proof: The country Zimbabwe has a mixture of languages; Shona, Ndebele, Venda, Manyika, Nyanja, Chagani, and a unique-unified Zimbabwean English.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Zimbabwe on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Zimbabwe on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Harare?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Zimbabwe is Harare.
